A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same FedFD study. All pages are readable, and the text, equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, learning curves, component ablations and sensitivity analyses in Sections 3.2 and 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results, including accuracy comparisons, communication-efficiency measurements and ablations in Sections 3.2 and 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same feature aggregation, architecture-specific projections, matrix-exponential orthogonalization and KL feature-distillation objective. No algorithm step or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet with the same test scenarios. The added mention of recommender systems is background context, not additional experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain HeteroFL, MOON-hetero, FedFusion-hetero, FedGen-hetero, DaFKD-hetero, FedMD, MSFKD and FedGD. The smaller comparator sets in Tables 4–6 and Figures 3–4 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented protocols remain unchanged, including Dirichlet partitioning, evaluation samples, 10 local epochs, 200 communication rounds, 20 clients, 0.4 participation, learning rates and model configurations. No experiment introduces a new evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Both retain the logit-distillation stability analysis, feature-alignment and orthogonal-projection ablations, model-combination sensitivity, scalability analysis and CNN/ResNet architecture check (Figure 3; Tables 3–6). No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same two-run procedure and summary calculations using each run's final ten rounds. Variability reporting and the tables' ± entries are unchanged; no seed or statistical procedure is added.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–6 and the plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports FedFD global CIFAR-10 accuracy of 89.64±0.23 at α=1.0 in both versions. No numerical or qualitative finding is added or revised.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1–9 are unchanged, including the matrix-exponential orthogonality derivation and distillation objective. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about feature distillation, orthogonal alignment, modularity, privacy, efficiency and superior accuracy. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of logit instability, generator training, component importance, scalability and architecture independence remain unchanged. No substantive limitation, applicability boundary or failure condition is added.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies the HPC Platform of Huazhong University of Science and Technology as the computing facility in its acknowledgments. This adds resource information without establishing a changed computational setup; implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds seven references, numbered 25–31, concerning federated recommendation and continual/incremental learning, and adjusts background citations in Sections 1–2. All earlier references remain. The central positioning relative to distillation methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations, corresponding-author and conference information, adds acknowledgments and a brief recommender-systems example. The main section order and nearly all scientific prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block and document reflow change placement: Algorithm 1 moves from page 5 to 6, while Table 2 and Figure 4 move from page 8 to 9. Figure content, captions and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly extends background context and funding/facility disclosure, but retains the same scientific argument, mathematical treatment, experiments, results and essentially the same exposition. These limited additions and layout changes do not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
